name: Ising
miniText: NetLogo Ising investigates how thermal noise competes with local spin alignment. Binary spins occupy a square lattice and selected spins flip according to their four-neighbor energy difference and a Metropolis acceptance probability. Introduces the spin-interaction problem underlying this model family [1]. Supplies the energy-dependent sampling mechanism used explicitly by the NetLogo Procedures [2]. Provides the two-dimensional equilibrium benchmark rather than a fit to this finite simulation [3]. The simulation assumes nearest-neighbor interactions, idealized spins and finite lattice size; update counts are computational time, not calibrated magnetic relaxation time. The simulation illustrates ordering, fluctuations and temperature-dependent magnetization. Reproducing these patterns establishes rule fidelity, not empirical validation.

Registrant abstract consulted: A general method, suitable for fast computing machines, for investigating such properties as equations of state for substances consisting of interacting individual molecules is described. The method consists of a modified Monte Carlo integration over configuration space. Results for the two-dimensional rigid-sphere system have been obtained on the Los Alamos MANIAC and are presented here. These results are compared to the free volume equation of state and to a four-term virial coefficient expansion.
